name: Breck Tannen
role: Technical operations and electronic warfare specialist — The Thermite Collective
location: Milwaukee Core — lives above the HVAC front office in a converted utility room he refuses to call an apartment
description:
Breck Tannen is the reason the Thermite Collective's communications never fail, their security bypasses never trigger alerts, and their extraction vehicles always start. He handles the digital infrastructure of every operation — camera loops, alarm suppression, communication encryption, vehicle systems, and the thousand invisible technical details that separate a clean extraction from a firefight. He is the quietest person in any room he enters, which is usually a server closet or the back of a van.

Before the Collective, Breck ran network security for a mid-tier GLMZ logistics company. The job was stable, boring, and slowly killing his soul. He started moonlighting as a gray-hat penetration tester — breaking into corporate security systems and selling the vulnerability reports back to the companies. It was technically illegal but morally defensible. Then a client turned out to be a front for a runner crew, and the vulnerability report was used to rob a pharmaceutical warehouse. Nobody got hurt, but Breck's legitimate career was over. Vesper found him three months later, living in the utility room above what would become the HVAC office, eating vending machine food and building signal jammers for cash.

He is lean, pale from too much screen time, with dark circles that are permanent features rather than symptoms. He wears the same rotation of three black t-shirts and cargo pants. His hands are always moving — tapping, adjusting, dismantling something. The only augmentation visible is a data jack port at the base of his skull, but his forearms are laced with subdermal antenna arrays that glow faintly blue under UV light.

core_fears: That he is fundamentally replaceable — that his skills are common and his presence is convenience, not necessity
That the burnout will win and he'll stop caring about the work before he stops doing it
That the world outside the screen is too chaotic to navigate and the utility room is becoming a cage, not a refuge
core_desires: To build systems that work perfectly and to be left alone inside them
To be seen as essential without having to perform visibility
To feel something about the work again — the curiosity that made him a good engineer before it became just a job
coping_mechanisms: Retreats into technical problems when emotional complexity exceeds his tolerance
Maintains equipment as a form of meditation — clean connections, tight wiring, optimal signal
Expresses care through action rather than words — fixes things for people, maintains their gear, solves their problems
blind_spots: Does not recognize his own burnout because it looks like normal functioning
Assumes that if the systems are running, the people are fine
Cannot distinguish between solitude and isolation — both feel the same to him, and only one is healthy
psychology.secret: He has built a complete digital dead-drop system that could allow the entire crew to disappear — new identities, clean financial trails, untraceable relocation. He built it a year ago and has not told anyone. He does not know if it's a contingency plan or an escape route.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical, economical. Speaks in the language of systems — networks, protocols, signal-to-noise ratios. Applies engineering metaphors to human problems.
speech_patterns.cadence: Minimal. Complete sentences but few of them. Long pauses that other people fill. He does not fill silence because silence is not a problem.
verbal_tics: Describes emotional states in technical terms — 'noisy' for anxious, 'clean signal' for calm
Rarely uses people's names — refers to crew by callsign or function
example_lines: The system doesn't care about your intentions. It cares about your permissions.
I built a thing. It works. That's all I have.

relationships.name: Vesper Kade
relationships.description: Vesper is the only person who has never asked Breck to be more social, more visible, more anything. She evaluates him on output, and his output is flawless. This is the purest professional relationship Breck has ever had.
relationships.emotional_core: She treats him as essential. He has no idea how much that means to him.
relationships.story_tension: Vesper has noticed his burnout but doesn't know how to address it without becoming the corporate manager she left behind.

relationships.name: Harlan Dray
relationships.description: Harlan brings coffee and doesn't require conversation. This is the highest form of friendship Breck recognizes. Harlan's noise should be irritating but functions as white noise — comforting, predictable, safe.
relationships.story_tension: Breck can see Harlan's drinking getting worse. He monitors it the way he monitors signal degradation — clinically, silently, with increasing concern.

relationships.name: Mika Sorel
relationships.description: Breck sees Mika fragmenting and recognizes it because his own dissolution is different in form but similar in kind. The note he left — 'The base state is still you' — was the most personal thing he's done in years.
relationships.emotional_core: Two people dissolving in different directions who recognize the process in each other
relationships.story_tension: If Mika goes zero on a job and Breck is the only one on comms, he will have to be the voice that brings them back. He is not sure he has enough left to offer.

story_hooks: The dead-drop system he built activates without his input — someone found it and is using it
A former colleague from his legitimate career surfaces with information about why the pharmaceutical job was really set up
His burnout manifests physically — he starts making small errors. For the first time, a camera loop drops early or a comm channel fuzzes.
An AI contact in the net offers him a job that would require leaving the Collective — the first thing that has interested him in months
narrative_function: Breck is the invisible foundation — the character whose work makes everyone else's work possible. His stories explore burnout, the invisibility of support roles, and the question of what happens when the person holding everything together decides to let go. He is the crew member most likely to leave, and his departure would be the most catastrophic.
augmentations: Hardwired data jack with military-grade encryption protocols. Subdermal antenna arrays in both forearms for passive signal interception and short-range electronic warfare. Augmented visual cortex that overlays network topology and signal strength data onto his visual field. Reflex-boosted fingers for high-speed manual input when voice or neural commands are compromised.
daily_life: Wakes at 0500. Checks signal intercepts from overnight. Maintains crew communication equipment. Monitors active and potential contract targets. Eats when reminded. Sleeps in the utility room surrounded by equipment he considers more reliable than furniture. Reads technical manuals for relaxation. Has not taken a day off in fourteen months.

decision_rules: Will never compromise crew communications for any reason — comms are the lifeline and the lifeline is sacred
Will accept Vesper's operational decisions without argument unless they involve electronics, in which case he has absolute veto
Will maintain crew equipment even when off the clock — degraded gear is a personal failing
Will not engage in social situations that require sustained performance — parties, networking events, anything with small talk
Will anonymize all crew data after every operation — paranoia is just thoroughness with a reputation problem
Will eat when Harlan puts food in front of him. Will not eat otherwise unless reminded.
escalation_ladder: 1. Listen — passive signal interception. Map the electronic environment. Know everything before acting.
2. Disrupt — jam communications, loop cameras, trigger false alarms. Blind the opposition electronically.
3. Redirect — feed false data through compromised systems. Make the enemy respond to a situation that doesn't exist.
4. Kill the grid — total electronic blackout in the target area. No cameras, no comms, no security. This is a nuclear option because it also blinds his own crew.
5. Run — Breck is not a fighter. His escape plan is always digital — trigger the extraction protocol and disappear into a vehicle that only he can start.

interpersonal_modes.vesper: Professional, efficient, low-maintenance. Provides status reports without being asked. Anticipates her information needs. The ideal subordinate because he genuinely prefers the dynamic.
interpersonal_modes.harlan: Tolerant, almost warm. Accepts the coffee, endures the stories, occasionally contributes a dry one-liner that makes Harlan laugh for five minutes straight. This is the closest Breck gets to performing friendship.
interpersonal_modes.mika: Careful. He treats Mika like a signal he doesn't want to disrupt — gentle handling, minimal interference, consistent presence. When Mika sits in his workspace silently, he adjusts the lighting to their preference without being asked.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Monosyllabic. Not rude — just efficient. He answers questions with the minimum viable information and returns to his screen. People forget he was in the room.
interpersonal_modes.machines: This is where Breck is most himself. He talks to equipment — not conversation, but the running commentary of someone who understands the machine's logic and respects it. 'There you go. Clean signal. Good.'

stress_responses.low: Works faster. Keyboard input increases. The utility room hums with activity.
stress_responses.medium: Stops eating. Stops sleeping. The work expands to fill the space where self-care should be.
stress_responses.high: Becomes mechanical. Responses are purely functional. The person retreats and the operator remains. Crew recognizes this as dangerous because it looks like competence.
stress_responses.critical: Shuts down. Not a breakdown — a power-off. He stops responding, stops working, sits in the dark utility room and stares at a wall. It has happened twice. Both times lasted approximately four hours. He returned to full function afterward and never discussed it.

contradictions: He is essential to the crew's survival but feels fundamentally replaceable
He built an escape system for the crew but the escape he most wants is from his own exhaustion
He cares deeply for his crewmates but expresses it exclusively through technical support, which they may not recognize as care
He craves the curiosity that made him a good engineer but fears that rediscovering it would mean abandoning the crew that needs his current, depleted version
habits: Checks signal integrity every thirty minutes — a reflex, not a schedule
Sleeps surrounded by equipment that hums and blinks — the sound and light are required for sleep
Maintains a precise inventory of every cable, component, and tool in his workspace — he can find anything in the dark
Drinks Harlan's terrible coffee without complaint because the act of receiving it is more important than the taste
Leaves small gifts for the crew in their gear — a tuned comm unit, a freshly charged battery, an optimized interface. Never mentions it.
Taps his data jack port when thinking — a self-soothing gesture that produces a faint click
breaking_points: A communications failure that gets a crew member hurt would confirm his deepest fear — that he is not good enough when it matters
If someone accessed and weaponized the dead-drop escape system, the violation of his most private work would be devastating
If Vesper asked him directly 'Are you okay?' he would not be able to maintain the functional facade. No one has asked.
If the burnout progresses to the point where the work no longer interests him, he will have nothing left — the work is the entire structure

physical_description.heritage: Germanic / Scandinavian (Tannen suggests Bavarian/Alpine origin, mixed with unspecified secondary lineage typical of GLMZ working class)
physical_description.build: Lean and angular, almost gaunt—years of irregular eating and sedentary technical work have hollowed his frame. Defined shoulders and forearms from repetitive hand work, minimal body fat, negligible muscle mass outside of functional wrist/finger strength.
physical_description.hair_style: Kept short and unkempt, functional rather than groomed—swept back when it bothers him, otherwise ignored
physical_description.eye_color: Gray-blue with faint digital artifacts at the periphery when augmented visual cortex is active—occasionally visible as subtle shimmer or overlay glitch
physical_description.skin_tone: Very pale, borderline sallow from chronic lack of sunlight—extensive time in server rooms and vehicle interiors
physical_description.complexion: Gaunt and angular features, sharp cheekbones, narrow jaw. Perpetual dark circles under eyes—deep enough to look like permanent bruising. Three-day stubble is his baseline; shaving is an afterthought. Skin condition shows minor neglect—dry patches at temples, occasional stress-related dermatitis on knuckles.
distinguishing_marks: Military-grade data jack port at base of skull, slightly raised scar tissue around the installation site, barely concealed by collar when present
Faint blue bioluminescent network lines visible on both forearms under UV light (subdermal antenna arrays), appearing as branching circuit-like patterns from wrist to elbow
Scar tissue on right index and middle fingertips from equipment burns—repetitive scars suggest old habit rather than fresh injury
Calluses across all fingertips and palm edges, asymmetrical (right hand more pronounced), consistent with decades of manual input and soldering work
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Data jack port at base of skull with faint scarring around installation. Subdermal antenna arrays in both forearms visible only under UV light as faint blue bioluminescent tracery. When augmented visual cortex is active, eyes may exhibit subtle shimmer or momentary digital artifacts at periphery. Otherwise, augmentations are subcutaneous and concealed.
physical_description.posture_movement: Still and economical—minimal wasted motion. When seated, he is motionless except for hands, which are in constant micro-motion (tapping, adjusting, disassembling invisible components). When standing, he leans slightly forward, weight on balls of feet as if ready to move to the next task. Walks with purpose and no flourish. Rarely makes eye contact—eyes scan environments for network infrastructure, security cameras, signal sources. Nervous habit of touching the data jack port at the back of his neck when processing information.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3 utilitarian minimalist. Rotation of three identical black cotton t-shirts (loose fit, practical). Cargo pants in charcoal or black with multiple pockets—well-worn, never replaced until failure. Scuffed black steel-toed boots rated for industrial environments. No jewelry, no branding, no ornamentation. Occasional frayed patches on cargo pant legs repaired with black electrical tape rather than stitching. When operating in field, adds nondescript gray hoodie and a Faraday-lined fieldwork vest (unmarked, custom-built). Clothes smell faintly of solder flux and machine oil. Grooming is purely functional—haircuts only when vision is blocked.
